source_caption:
Troy turned Greek mythology into a massive cinematic spectacle, but what still makes the film memorable is Brad Pitt’s performance as Achilles. His physical transformation, intensity, and screen presence gave the character a larger-than-life feeling that matched the legend itself. Even years later, Achilles remains one of Pitt’s most iconic roles.

Directed by Wolfgang Petersen and inspired by Homer’s Iliad, the film follows the conflict between Troy and the Greek armies, focusing on pride, revenge, honor, and the pursuit of immortality through legacy. The duel between Achilles and Hector, played by Eric Bana, is still considered one of the best choreographed sword fights in modern epic cinema.

Historically, the film takes plenty of liberties. It removes most of the mythology and gods from Homer’s original story, grounding the events in a more realistic war drama instead of full fantasy. While historians often criticized the armor, timelines, and simplified politics of the Trojan War, the movie was never aiming for complete historical accuracy as much as emotional scale and mythic storytelling. 

Interestingly, Christopher Nolan was briefly attached to direct Troy before the project ultimately went to Wolfgang Petersen. Years later, Nolan said his early interest in Greek mythology and the Trojan War never fully left him, themes he would revisit with his later adaptation of The Odyssey.

source_details.synopsis: Troy is a 2004 epic historical action film directed by Wolfgang Petersen and written by David Benioff. Produced by units in Malta, Mexico, and Britain's Shepperton Studios, the film features an ensemble cast led by Brad Pitt, Eric Bana, Orlando Bloom, Diane Kruger, Sean Bean, Brian Cox, Brendan Gleeson, Rose Byrne, and Peter O'Toole. It is loosely based on Homer's Iliad in its narration of the entire story of the decade-long Trojan War—condensed into little more than a couple of weeks, rather than just the quarrel between Achilles and Agamemnon in the ninth year.
